text:
incident-bot: Pager: detected sustained errors in serving (region: eu-west) on gpu-v2-prod pool. symptoms aggregated: CUDA_TIMEOUT (kernel_watchdog), ibv_post_send failures, container OOMKills. 5xx spike to 12% over 1m, p50 latency from 120ms -> 2.4s. root ts 1824012345
Maya: i'm oncall, ack. i'm pulling logs + will page runtime on-call. tagging @Jordan @Lee
Jordan: on it. just checked alerts — node-13 and node-14 show interface flaps at 1824012338-1824012350. also seeing CUDA watchdog resets in the same pods. possible cascading: IB packet drops -> hung kernels -> OOMs when tasks queue
Lee: adding context from runtime: when RDMA sends fail we fall back to host memcpy which increases memory pressure and stalls KV cache. if many requests queue the allocator can OOM containers. sending diagnostic commands now.
Maya: can we confirm impacted customers / routes? Priya from support, do you have customer reports?
Priya: support seeing ~7 tickets from EU test accounts and 3 production customers complaining about 5xx and long tails. not all are same model, but all routed through gpu-v2-prod. raising severity to sev2 for now.
Jordan: pasting recent pod log snippets from pod serving-abc-7f6dd (node-13):
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] runtime: cuda: kernel watchdog timeout on device 0
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] runtime: kernel reset triggered, context lost
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] rdma: ibv_post_send failed: EINVAL (invalid argument)
[2026-03-15T08:12:33Z] serving: request handler stalled, queued=412
[2026-03-15T08:12:35Z] oomkiller: containerd: killed process 2345 (serve) total_mem: 31.2GiB
```
Jordan: also seeing system dmesg on node-13: "mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: netdev: ib device reset due to link err"
Lee: thanks. i'm running ibstat and mlx5 counters across the rack. preliminary shows port 2 on HCA0 with link down->up flaps ~20 times in 2m and RX errors increasing.
Maya: immediate mitigation plan?
Lee: recommended quick mitigations: 1) fail traffic off node-13/14 (cordon + drain pods with immediate replacement), 2) enable TCP fallback for the serving pool for new requests (route-policy temporary), 3) reduce batch sizes to lower memory pressure, 4) restart affected GPUs' drivers after drain.
Maya: i'll cordon node-13 now. Jordan, can you push route change to send new sessions to eu-fallback (cpu or smaller model)?
Jordan: on it. running: `rbw routing set --pool gpu-v2-prod --fallback eu-fallback --weight 1.0 --reason "RDMA flaps"`
Jordan: applied. returning 503s to caller if no fallback available for now to avoid pile-up.
Priya: communicating to customers: sending status update that we see networking-induced GPU outages, mitigation in progress, ETA 30-60m.
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: Maya -> Ryan at 1824012400. please acknowledge when you pick up.
Ryan: ack, i'll be standby for next steps.
Lee: after cordon/drain, noticed pods restarted on other nodes but some get stuck in CrashLoopBackOff due to init cache warmup memory peak. lowering batch by setting env SERVE_BATCH_MAX=4 on deployment to reduce warmup. applying patch now.
Maya: patch applied to canary subset. monitoring metrics.
Jordan: kubectl output for one of affected pods: `kubectl describe pod serving-abc-7f6dd -n serving` shows 4 restarts in 2m and events: Back-off restarting failed container, OOMKilled.
Maya: after route change + batch limit, 5xx dropped from 12% -> 3.2% in 5m, latency p50 back to 160ms, p95 still elevated.
Lee: discovered firmware mismatch on node-14 HCA during quick compare. scheduling hotfix with infra: firmware rollback/upgrade is required. for now keeping nodes cordoned.
Priya: customers acknowledged interim update; one enterprise customer asked for timeline for failed requests and potential data loss — answered: no data loss, requests returned 5xx for retries, suggest they retry after 10s.
Jordan: we're going to keep TCP fallback enabled for next 30m and monitor. if stable, we'll gradually uncordon nodes after firmware check + driver restart.
Maya: runtime note: also saw one container crash with CUDA_UNKNOWN_ERROR in stack trace after ib reset — that tends to mean driver needing a clean restart, so we'll full reboot GPU drivers on affected hosts during maintenance window.
oncall-bot: Reminder: escalate to Eng Infra if hardware persists.
Lee: action items created: (1) firmware sync on HCA across rack (owner: Lee), (2) driver restart + kernel patch verification on node-13/14 (owner: Infra), (3) follow-up to add better backpressure when RDMA degrades (owner: Runtime eng), (4) add alert for rdma RX err threshold (owner: SRE).
Maya: verifying customer impact one more time — current 5xx at 0.9% cluster-wide, eu pool 2.1%. continuing to monitor.
Ryan: taking over oncall at 1824012400, thanks @Maya. i'm watching metrics + oncall channel.
Maya: handing off docs: added notes to incident doc: `/incidents/1824012345` and flagged for postmortem.
Priya: prepping customer-facing postmortem blurb: short summary + steps taken + mitigation + next steps. will sync postmortem draft when incident closed.
Lee: final status at 1824012480: nodes cordoned, traffic routed to fallback, 5xx under 1%, ops plan scheduled for 02:00 UTC to perform firmware and driver maintenance, follow-up postmortem assigned.
Maya: closing pager for now, keeping thread open for postmortem discussions. reactions: :thumbsup:
